raw_response:
I will keep doing what fits my land and water best here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the safest way for me to use the whole year, spread labor across seasons, and protect my income. Wheat is familiar, easy for me to manage with the habits and tools I already know, and maize after wheat makes full use of the summer heat and rains. I will not split my land into too many crops because that makes management harder and raises risk. I will prepare the wheat land with rotary tillage, use improved seed, put most of the fertilizer in at sowing and then add nitrogen again later if the crop needs it. For maize, I will sow soon after wheat harvest, keep the field clean, irrigate when the rain is not enough, and use pesticide only when pests or disease pressure show up. My goal is steady yield, lower risk, and work I know I can finish on time.
